hook.line: Tomás has to cross the whole city tomorrow, and Vale is not the kind of friend who says "you might want to consider". She just tells him what to do. Spanish makes that easy: you already know the form.
hook.es: Sal temprano, toma el bus en la esquina y paga con la tarjeta.
hook.en: Leave early, catch the bus at the corner and pay with the card.

rule:
To tell a friend what to do, take the he/she form of the present and use it as it is:
*Vale toma el bus.* Vale takes the bus.
*Tomás, toma el bus.* Tomás, take the bus.

So *mira*, *espera*, *come*, *cruza*, *paga*. If the verb changes its middle, the command does too: *sigue*, *vuelve*, *duerme*.

Eight everyday verbs are short and irregular. Learn them as a set:
*ven* (come), *ten* (have, take), *pon* (put), *sal* (leave)
*haz* (do, make), *di* (say), *ve* (go), *sé* (be)
The first four are just the verb with its ending chopped off: *venir*, *ven*.

Like English, there's no word for "you" in front. A name with a comma tells you it's an instruction: *Tomás, toma el bus.*

This is only for "do it". "Don't do it" uses a different form, coming later.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the affirmative *tú* imperative. Its regular form is the same as the third person singular of the present.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Ven* or *Vienes* and type the whole sentence: *___ mañana a las ocho.* (Come tomorrow at eight, to a friend.)
yourTurn.why: It's an instruction, and *venir* is one of the eight short ones: *ven*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Sal* or *Sales* and type the whole sentence: *___ temprano.* (Leave early, to a friend.)
yourTurn.why: *Sales* is "you leave". The instruction is the short form, *sal*.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a friend: Look at this.
yourTurn.why: *Mira* is "she looks", and to a friend it also means "look".

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a friend: Catch the bus at the corner.
yourTurn.answer: Toma el bus en la esquina.
yourTurn.why: Catching a bus is *tomar*, and the command is *toma*.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell Tomás to wait a moment. Start with his name.
yourTurn.why: The name and the comma, then *espera*: the he/she form used as an instruction.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn this into an instruction to a friend: *Comes algo.*
yourTurn.why: Drop the *s* of "you eat" and you have "eat".

yourTurn.prompt: Turn this into an instruction to a friend: *Pones el celular en la mesa.*
yourTurn.answer: Pon el celular en la mesa.
yourTurn.why: *Poner* is one of the short ones: *pon*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn this into an instruction to a friend: *Sigues dos cuadras.*
yourTurn.why: *Sigue* keeps the *i* it has in *sigues*; only the *s* goes.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Tomas* means "you take"; the instruction drops the *s*.
*Venir* is one of the eight short ones: just *ven*.
*Hace* is "he makes". To a friend, the instruction is *haz*.
*Seguir* changes its middle to *i*, and the command keeps it: *sigue*.

personal: Give a friend three instructions to get from your door to the nearest bus stop or café. Try *sal*, *camina* and *cruza*.
